text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Friday, it has removed the short-term, long-term and legal ratings of Industri & Skipsbanken (ISB) from RatingWatch with positive implications.

"Following ISB's merger with Finansbanken AS on December 30 1996, the new bank is to be known as Finansbanken ASA and its ratings are affirmed at A3 short-term, BBB long-term and an individual rating of C," IBCA said in a statement.
The legal rating has been changed to 4 from 5.

"Both have experienced periods of uncertainty over the past two years but IBCA anticipates that the merger will be positive for the new bank and will enable it to compete more effectively with larger Norwegian banks in its target areas," IBCA said.
Asset quality appears sound and lending is well secured IBCA said, although loan concentrations in some sectors may need to be reduced, it said.
The new bank had a pro forma core capital/weighted risks ratio of 8.96 percent at end-September 1996 which seems adequate, although not exceptionally high, for a small niche bank, IBCA said.
